Dalawang Mabuhay Lane routes ang tinarget ng Swift Traffic Action Group sa operasyon ng grupo ngayong araw.

Sinuyod ng STAG ang West Avenue sa kahabaan ng EDSA QC, Del Monte, Biak na Bato, Ma. Clara, Blumentritt na pawang mga nasa Quezon City gayundin ang M. dela Fuente at Vicente Cruz sa Manila.

Nasa 105 ang nahuli sa ilalim ng No Contact Apprehension o ang panghuhuli sa pamamagitan ng body-worn cameras habang 34 naman ang physical apprehension na pawang mga motoristang may paglabag sa dress code o di kaya'y walang helmet.

Mahalagang obstruction-free ang mga Mabuhay Lane na nagsisilbing alternatibong ruta para mas maging maayos at tuloy-tuloy ang daloy ng trapiko at makatulong na mapaluwag ang volume ng mga sasakyan sa mga pangunahing lansangan gaya ng EDSA.

The Criminal Investigation and Detection Group said on Monday it issued subpoenas against four alleged leaders of groups in connection with the reported violent incidents in Manila during the September 21 protest against corruption.

“Nag-issue po ng subpoena ang CIDG sa apat na indibidwal, allegedly leaders ng apat din na grupo na allegedly may kinalaman sa violent incident,” CIDG spokesperson Police Major Helen dela Cruz said in a press briefing.

The CIDG will file a petition for indirect contempt of court for those who failed to comply with the subpoena, according to the spokesperson.

data.text:
Resignation as a Moral Stand: Lessons from France, Reflections for the Philippines
By Dr. Tony Leachon

In France, newly appointed Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu resigned in less than a month—just hours after forming his cabinet—amid threats from allies and foes alike. It was a swift, sobering decision. 

A recognition that leadership, when compromised, must yield to principle.

Here in the Philippines, Senator Ping Lacson’s planned resignation from the Blue Ribbon Committee echoes a similar moral clarity. It is not weakness—it is a protest against obstruction, politicization, and the erosion of institutional trust. 

Like Lecornu, Lacson is choosing dignity over power, truth over position.

But resignation alone cannot cleanse a system. It must be followed by accountability from those who remain.

President Marcos Jr. must confront the corruption that festers under his watch. He cannot feign ignorance while former Speaker Martin Romualdez remains untouched, and Zaldy Co disappears without consequence. 

The budget he signed is now seen as the most compromised in history. The buck stops at his table.

If the Independent Commission on Infrastructure (ICI) fails to act with urgency and transparency, it risks becoming a shield for the powerful—not a sword for the people. Livestream the hearings. Name the masterminds. Jail the guilty.

Resignation may be honorable. But action is indispensable.

Let us not lose momentum. Let us not lose faith. Let reform begin—not in silence, but in sunlight.

#RelentlessForChange
@Reuters @gmanews @24OrasGMA @dzbb
